sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that the applicant and the victim have solemnized marriage with each other.
It is argued that the incident of rape is alleged to have taken place on 08.12.2022 but the present FIR has been lodged on 09.10.2023 which is after a period of about 10 months.
It is argued that the investigation in the matter is under progress.

It is argued that the marriage of the applicant with the informant is a registered marriage regarding which a certificate of registration has been issued by the Marriage Registration Officer of the said marriage which registered on 09.12.2022.

It is argued that there has been some dispute between the applicant and the informant after marriage and then the applicant has filed a case under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act before the concerned Family court on 07.10.2023 subsequent to which the present FIR has been lodged.
It is argued that a joint petition under Section 13(B) of the Hindu Marriage Act has been filed by the applicant and the informant before the concerned court which is also pending.
It is further argued that the applicant has no criminal history as stated in para 31 of the affidavit.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.

7. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the applicant and the first informant solemnized marriage which was duly registered before the Marriage Registration Officer.
A case under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act was filed by the applicant against the first informant after which the First Information Report has been lodged.
A joint petition under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act has been filed by the applicant and the informant.
The FIR has been lodged after 10 months of the alleged incident.
8. Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, considering the nature of accusation, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case.

9. In the event of arrest of the applicant- Dhirendra Chaudhary, involved in aforesaid case crime no.
shall be released on anticipatory bail during pendency of trial on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) the applicant shall make himself available on each and every date fixed in the matter by the court concerned.

(ii) the applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court.
(iii) the applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if he has passport the same shall be deposited by him before the concerned court.
